title: Grateful Dead Live at Capital Centre on 1982-09-15
lineage: CDR > EAC > WavMerge > Soundforge (on d2t12) > CD-Wave > TLH v.1.0.0.72 (for SBE-OK, FLAC compression, and checksums) > FLAC
source: "Recorded by Tiger Rose, FOB Nak shotgun mics > Sony TC-D5. MAC > CD Analog to Digital transfer by David Howard."

ai_review.summary: A superb front‑of‑house recording that captures a smoking Crazy Fingers, tight Shakedown, the first Touch of Grey encore and a wild space‑jam into NFA with crystal‑clear sound.
ai_review.review: This show is praised for its high energy and creative setlist – standout moments include Crazy Fingers, a solid Shakedown, the historic first Touch of Grey encore and an intense space‑jam that folds into No Fixed Address.  The recording, captured by Tiger Rose, delivers front‑of‑house clarity that many reviewers say feels like sitting in the 15th row, making it one of the best early‑80s FOB tapes available.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of nine detailed reviews are 4–5 stars and highlight both an energetic performance and excellent sound quality, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the tape as crisp, on‑stage sounding, with ambience that puts the listener near the front row; no significant dropouts or muddiness are mentioned.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A unique, well‑played first set followed by a second set that builds from Shakedown into a brief Playing jam, solid Sailor/Saint segment, strong Drums and an inventive space jam leading into NFA; overall flow praised despite a missing reprise of the Playing jam.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is repeatedly praised, especially on Crazy Fingers and throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: One reviewer noted the show was great up to the drums but felt the drum segment was only average.
